title: Daily Fleece Quiz App — Project Handover
description:
Quiz app for daily standup fun. Two questions per session: Q1 (knowledge, A/B/C) and Q2 (geography, select country on map). Both presented as uploaded photos (calendar page photo for Q1, location photo for Q2).

KEY DOCUMENTS:
- REQUIREMENTS.md — 9 use cases (UC-01 to UC-09) + 20 functional requirements
- CONTEXT.md — domain glossary (Session, Host, Player, Lobby, Voting, Answer, etc.)
- docs/adr/0001-0009 — Architecture Decision Records

DOMAIN SUMMARY:
- Host = first player to tap 'Start Quiz'; also plays as a regular player
- Session phases: Lobby → Active → Ended
- Two questions per session, Q1 then Q2, host controls pacing
- Voting: hidden until host closes it; host sees count only ('4/6 answered')
- Players can change answer while voting open; non-answering = 0 pts
- 1 pt per correct answer; host marks correct answer after closing voting
- Session locked after start (lobby-only joining)
- Running leaderboard, always accessible, one global project for now

STACK (decided):
- Monorepo: api/, backend/, frontend/
- Backend: Spring Boot + Java, Spring Modulith (2 modules: quiz + player)
- Frontend: Angular, NgRx Signal Store, Sheriff, Testing Library
- Datastores: MongoDB (primary + GridFS for photos) + Valkey (live session state)
- API: spec-first OpenAPI in api/openapi.yaml
- Deploy: 2 CF apps (nginx buildpack + java buildpack)
- Photo TTL: 28 days via MongoDB GridFS TTL index
- Auth: stub (name-based) now, company SSO (OIDC) later
- Mobile-first

DEFERRED:
- Real-time protocol (SSE vs WebSocket) — pending intranet network check
- Auth implementation details — pending company SSO specifics
- Project management / leaderboard reset — one global project for now
close_reason: Handover context now lives in REQUIREMENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, docs/adr/, and bd memory. Codebase is the source of truth.

title: Decide real-time protocol: SSE vs WebSocket
description:
The quiz requires server-to-client push: question opens, voting closes, answer revealed, scores updated.

SSE + REST (recommended): Server pushes via long-lived HTTP stream. Clients send actions via REST. Simpler, fits OpenAPI contract cleanly.
WebSocket (STOMP): Full-duplex, Spring first-class support. More complex.

BLOCKED ON: Check company intranet restrictions — corporate proxies may block WebSockets or long-lived HTTP. Once known, pick one and write ADR-0007.

Real-time events endpoint TBD (depends on protocol decision). Country = ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.

title: SSO cutover: confirm JWT subject vs Company ID for identity linking
description:
Stub auth model (decided 2026-05-29): Player has an app-generated opaque playerId (surrogate key used by sessions + leaderboard) PLUS a unique Company ID the user types as a recovery natural key. registerPlayer is get-or-create keyed on Company ID. At SSO cutover we add a 'subject' field and link the JWT sub to the existing Player — the app-generated playerId is preserved, so sessions/leaderboard are never rekeyed.

OPEN QUESTION (external fact, sibling of df-lg7): we do not yet know whether the JWT 'sub' equals the Company ID (t...a employee id) or some other identifier (opaque directory GUID, email, OIDC pairwise id). 

BLOCKED ON: knowing the IdP/JWT claim shape. If sub != Company ID AND the IdP exposes no Company ID claim, linking existing records needs a manual/backfill mapping. Mitigation already in place: the surrogate playerId means the blast radius is a one-time link/backfill over ~20 rows, not a rekey. Decide once the JWT claim shape is known.
